How to use

  • Use one drop at a time. This is the most concentrated thing we sell.
  • Dilute to 1% or less — it is overwhelming above that.
  • Blend a single drop into sandalwood for a classic Indian pairing.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

Who it's for

Anyone who grew up with mogra

The smell of jasmine garlands, concentrated to the point of being almost overwhelming.

Perfume blenders

A heart note of real depth, and one drop is enough to change an entire blend.

Occasion rather than everyday

Priced and concentrated as something you reach for deliberately, not daily.

What people get wrong

Using more than one drop. This is the most concentrated material we sell. At two drops a blend stops smelling of jasmine and starts smelling of too much jasmine, and there is no recovering it.

Expecting an essential oil. Jasmine cannot be steam distilled without destroying the scent, so every jasmine on the market is an absolute, extracted with solvents. That is inherent to the material, not a shortcut.

What it won't do

As an absolute it carries trace solvent residue by nature of the process. If you only use steam-distilled oils, this is not for you.

Jasmine sambac, grandiflorum and auriculatum are three different species sold under one name, and they smell meaningfully different.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Jasmine Sambac (Mogra) Absolute

Why is jasmine an absolute rather than an essential oil?

The flowers are too delicate for steam distillation — the heat destroys exactly the compounds you want. Solvent extraction is the only way to capture the scent, which is why all jasmine is sold as an absolute.

Is this the same as mogra?

Yes. Mogra is the common Indian name for Jasminum sambac, the species used in garlands across the country. Grandiflorum is the species more often used in European perfumery and smells greener.

Why is it so expensive?

The flowers are picked by hand at night, when the scent peaks, and must be processed within hours. It takes an enormous quantity of flowers to produce a few millilitres of absolute.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Lower than most. An absolute, not an essential oil — it is solvent extracted, so trace residue is inherent to the process. Avoid during pregnancy. For general use, dilute into a carrier oil such as jojoba and patch-test on a small area first.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.

How quickly will it arrive?

Orders are dispatched from Delhi within two business days and usually arrive within a further three to five, depending on where you are. Shipping is free over ₹999.
